title: sieve-native: evaluator — RFC 5228 core commands and tests
description:
Implement the evaluator that walks a Script (Vec<Stmt>) and dispatches on command names. All Sieve knowledge lives here — the parser knows nothing.

What: src/evaluator.rs + src/message.rs

Evaluation model:
  A Script is a Vec<Stmt>. Each Stmt is a Vec<Form> whose first element is always Word(name).
  The evaluator dispatches on the name string:

  fn eval_stmt(stmt: &Stmt, ctx: &mut Ctx) -> StmtResult
    match stmt.as_slice() {
      [Word(cmd), rest @ ..] => match cmd.as_str() {
        "require"  => check_extensions(rest),
        "if"       => eval_if(rest, ctx),
        "fileinto" => eval_fileinto(rest, ctx),
        "reject"   => eval_reject(rest, ctx),
        "discard"  => Ok(StmtResult::Discard),
        "keep"     => Ok(StmtResult::Keep),
        "stop"     => Ok(StmtResult::Stop),
        "set"      => eval_set(rest, ctx),     // variables extension
        other       => Err(UnknownCommand(other)),
      }
    }

  fn eval_test(stmt: &Stmt, ctx: &Ctx) -> bool
    match stmt.as_slice() {
      [Word("header"),   rest @ ..] => eval_header_test(rest, ctx),
      [Word("address"),  rest @ ..] => eval_address_test(rest, ctx),
      [Word("envelope"), rest @ ..] => eval_envelope_test(rest, ctx),
      [Word("exists"),   rest @ ..] => eval_exists_test(rest, ctx),
      [Word("size"),     rest @ ..] => eval_size_test(rest, ctx),
      [Word("allof"),    rest @ ..] => eval_allof(rest, ctx),
      [Word("anyof"),    rest @ ..] => eval_anyof(rest, ctx),
      [Word("not"),      rest @ ..] => !eval_test(&rest[0], ctx),
      [Word("true")]               => true,
      [Word("false")]              => false,
      _                             => false,   // unknown test = false (fail-safe)
    }

  Tags are just Form::Tag values in the rest slice — extract them with a helper:
    fn take_tag<'a>(rest: &'a [Form], name: &str) -> Option<(&'a Form, &'a [Form])>
  This is the entire dispatch mechanism. No match arms for grammar structure.

  eval_if(rest): rest = [test_stmt, Block(then), optionally Block(else)]
    Pull first Stmt from rest → run eval_test.
    Pull Block(then) → eval_stmt_list if true.
    Look for Word("elsif") or Word("else") in remaining rest.

message.rs:
  fn extract_headers(raw: &[u8]) -> Vec<(String, String)>   // scan up to first blank line; fold continuations
  fn address_part(value: &str, part: &Form) -> &str          // Form::Tag("localpart"|"domain"|"all")

Comparator helpers (no external crate):
  fn matches_is(a: &str, b: &str, casemap: bool) -> bool
  fn matches_contains(haystack: &str, needle: &str, casemap: bool) -> bool
  fn matches_glob(value: &str, pattern: &str, casemap: bool) -> bool  // * = any, ? = one, \* \? = literal

pub fn compile(script: &[u8]) -> Result<CompiledScript, String>   → tokenize + read_script; check require decls
pub fn evaluate(script: &CompiledScript, ...) -> Vec<SieveAction> → build Ctx, eval_stmt_list, append Keep if no disposition

Defensive rules:
  - Scan headers only (stop at blank line); never read body.
  - Unknown extension in require → compile error.
  - Malformed address → treat address-part as empty string.
  - No unwrap() in production paths.
notes:
**Regex extension (draft-ietf-sieve-regex)**

Add alongside the RFC 5228 match types. sieve-rs uses fancy-regex (supports lookahead/lookbehind); use the same crate so the cross-validation oracle produces identical results on edge-case patterns.

Cargo.toml addition: fancy-regex = "0.13"

Changes to evaluator.rs:
1. Add MatchType::Regex to the match type enum (or handle inline as a Tag variant).
2. In take_match_type(): Tag("regex") → MatchType::Regex.
3. In the comparator dispatch:
     MatchType::Regex => matches_regex(value, pattern, casemap)
4. fn matches_regex(value: &str, pattern: &str, casemap: bool) -> bool
     Build fancy_regex::Regex from pattern (case-insensitive flag if casemap).
     Return regex.is_match(value).unwrap_or(false).

Compile-time validation (in compile()):
   After parse, walk the Script and for every Stmt containing Tag("regex") as a match type, extract the pattern Str(s) and call fancy_regex::Regex::new(s). If Err, return compile error with the pattern and error message. Bad regex patterns are caught at upload time, not at first message evaluation.

require ["regex"] must be declared; compile error if :regex used without it.

Add "regex" to known_extensions list alongside "fileinto" and "variables".
